You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-282 "Cart Out of Stock and Partial Out of Stock". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §5/§6 is directly relevant: buffer-threshold-driven OOS states (CAI-026/027/028), NO soft reservation at add-to-cart, hard reservation only at order placement (CAI-032), cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart with NO auto-removal (CAI-035/036), Checkout CTA disabled if OOS at checkout entry.
- CRITICAL, CONFIRMED, LIVE BACKEND GAP (CAI-034, cart.md §6 and its Open Items §12): "Real-time inventory check via NewStore/MuleSoft when customer proceeds from cart → checkout entry... a new MuleSoft flow is required as none currently exists." Direct quote from the requirement's own open comment: "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." This means TRUE real-time OOS detection at the cart→checkout boundary is not buildable today — only the slower periodic inventory feed (15-min delta per CAI-020) is available. This is a hard, named API/backend dependency — flag it explicitly, don't soften it.
- A separate ticket in this batch, SFCC-796 "Cart Page Product Unavailable", may substantially overlap with this one — check for the actual distinction (e.g. stock-depletion-driven "Out of Stock" vs. a fully discontinued/removed-from-catalogue "Unavailable" product, which pdp.md's PRD-010 treats as a different state).

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-282', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-796 (description only is fine) for the overlap check.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies — name the CAI-034 gap explicitly here? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (does the ticket expect real-time detection, or is it scoped to the feed-based interim behaviour — check the AC directly), desktop/mobile, a11y (stock-change notification needs a live region), data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Design dependency: does a design exist for full-OOS vs. partial-OOS states?
6. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- The CAI-034 MuleSoft-gap flag: does this ticket's AC assume real-time detection that isn't buildable yet, or is it correctly scoped to feed-based behaviour? Say which, and if unclear, say that.
- The overlap check against SFCC-796
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

34	## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)
35	
36	- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**

43	## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)
44	
45	- Wishlist requires authentication — guests attempting to save are redirected to login (CAI-018)

48	- Shareable via email

55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)
56	
57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
61	- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

63	### Buffer stock
64	- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
65	- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.

70	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)

74	- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
75	- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened

81	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart

90	
91	- Button shown on PDP for eligible products
92	- Opens as a flyout panel (CAI-037)
93	- On open: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft once a size has been selected (the call is per-size and refreshes when the customer selects a different size — CAI-038)
94	- No auto-refresh while the flyout panel is open
95	- Per-boutique availability for the currently selected size: **In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock** (CAI-039)

103	## 8. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CAI-043 – CAI-045)
104	
105	*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*
106	
107	- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)
108	- On order placement, the order is submitted to NewStore OMS with the selected boutique as the fulfilment location; NewStore routes and assigns to boutique staff (CAI-044)
109	- Collect in Boutique availability responses cached on initial OMS call, refreshed on TTL expiry; TTL configurable in Business Manager (CAI-045)
110	
111	---

113	## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)
114	
115	- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
116	- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
117	- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
118	- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers

122	## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)
123	
124	- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
125	- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
126	- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
127	- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")

131	## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)
132	
133	- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
134	- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)

138	## 12. Open Items
139	
140	- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". The AC-vs-PRD conflict on Checkout CTA state (disabled per PRD vs "visually enabled but backend-blocked" per AC) is central enough that I want to check the attached mockups directly rather than rely on text alone.

## SFCC-282 — Backlog Refinement Notes

**One-line summary:** SFCC-282 specifies cross-component cart behaviour for fully-OOS and partial-OOS (limited-stock) line items — banner/inline/order-summary error messaging, stepper disable states, and Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay CTA blocking — but it is explicitly *not* a component-build story, and its own AC text conflicts with both the PRD requirement it's labelled against and its own attached design mockup on the one question that matters most: whether the Checkout CTA is disabled or "visually enabled but backend-blocked."

Ticket facts: Story, Priority High, status **Tech design** (To Do), parent Epic SFCC-11 "Cart" (To Do), assignee Victor T. Crisostomo, reporter Isabel Chaloner, labels `CAI-036`/`Custom`/`Squad-A`, **no Sprint assigned, no story-point estimate** — genuinely ungroomed. Created 2026-07-31; PO (Emma Kirwan) signed off on functional behaviour 2026-08-31 with one request (make error copy explicitly configurable); Isabel Chaloner added AC14 to satisfy that and noted a "PO approved" tag on 2026-09-01 — though that tag doesn't actually appear in the current labels field, worth a quick manual check in the Jira UI. Status has stayed at "Tech design" throughout, i.e. it hasn't moved past PO sign-off into a "ready for dev" state.

---

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact?** Yes, entirely — this is composed FE state/behaviour across up to four components (cart item, error banner, order summary, button group).
2. **Requirement clear enough to size?** Partially. 14 ACs (7 Full-OOS, 6 Partial-OOS, 1 error-copy) are specific and testable for the messaging/stepper-disable/clear-on-remove logic. The Checkout-CTA-state AC (AC5, AC10) is not safely sizeable as written — see behaviour axis below.
3. **Which surfaces?** Unclear. The description says the banner renders "at the top of the **cart drawer**," and the attached mockups are a "BAG" drawer panel (X-close, no page chrome) — matching cart.md §1 Mini-Cart. But 3 of its 4 dependency tickets are titled "**Cart Page** – ..." (SFCC-274, SFCC-275), and the mockup includes an "ADD PROMOTION CODE" row, which cart.md §2 (CAI-011) scopes to the Cart Page only, not the Mini-Cart (§1 has no promo-code bullet). Whether this story covers mini-cart only, full cart page only, or both isn't stated.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Design exists — see Design status below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Yes — the CAI-034 gap applies directly; see flag below.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** Shared FE/BE at minimum (SFCC must already be evaluating buffer-threshold state per cart.md §5 for the FE to render against), and the Checkout-CTA-blocking mechanism specifically needs an architecture decision before FE can safely build it.
7. **Size now or clarify first?** Clarify first — see readiness call.

---

### Four standing axes

- **Behaviour:** All 14 ACs are scoped to "when the cart renders" — i.e., re-evaluating already-known/synced inventory state, consistent with the feed-based interim behaviour, not a live per-click check. That part is internally consistent with what's buildable today. But AC5/AC10's "blocked at backend level from processing" for Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay (a) doesn't say what backend call this is, (b) doesn't say what the shopper sees/experiences on click — no error message or feedback path specified in any AC, and (c) directly conflicts with the PRD requirement this ticket is labelled against (cart.md §6, **CAI-036**: *"Checkout CTA is disabled"*) and with its own attached mockup (see below).
- **Desktop/mobile:** Not addressed. Only one layout is attached (wide, two-column "BAG" drawer view). No mobile/narrow-viewport mockup, no responsive-specific AC.
- **A11y:** Not addressed in any AC. Three dynamically-appearing status surfaces (inline message, page banner, order-summary message) have no `aria-live`/`role="alert"`/`role="status"` requirement specified anywhere — a WCAG 2.2 AA gap (4.1.3 Status Messages: must be programmatically announced without a focus change). This needs a live region per AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target.
- **Data:** The buffer-threshold OOS/limited-stock signal itself (cart.md §5, CAI-024–028, fed by the 15-min delta per CAI-020) is presumably what drives this, but the ticket doesn't confirm the trigger/timing for re-evaluation (on cart open only? on every render? polled?) — genuinely unclear, not stated anywhere in the AC.

---

### Design status

**Exists**, for both states. Two reference PNGs are attached directly to the ticket (Isabel Chaloner, 2026-08-25) and the description links a specific Figma frame (`Zimmermann Designs`, node-id `7383-167057`) plus the Design System UI Kit (node-id `2129-19977`). I opened the two attached images directly (they read as the export of that same frame) rather than the live Figma file. Visually confirmed against the AC text:
- Stepper states match exactly: Full-OOS shows both `−`/`+` greyed (AC3); Partial-OOS shows only `+` greyed with `−` active (AC10).
- Banner and inline/order-summary error copy match in spirit (exact wording differs slightly, e.g. "This is unavailable" vs AC1's "This item is unavailable" — immaterial given AC14 makes copy configurable).
- **The Checkout button is rendered in a visually greyed-out/disabled style in both mockups, while Apple Pay and Google Pay appear in their normal, fully-enabled styling.** This directly contradicts AC5/AC10's claim that "the Checkout CTA, Apple Pay and Google Pay Express buttons remain visually enabled" — only 2 of the 3 buttons the AC describes actually look enabled in the design. No mobile/narrow-viewport variant is attached or linked anywhere.

---

### CAI-034 MuleSoft-gap flag

**Unclear, leaning toward "correctly scoped to feed-based, but not stated explicitly."** The ticket makes **zero mention** of MuleSoft, NewStore, real-time checks, or the inventory feed anywhere in its text. Its ACs are all keyed off "when the cart renders" (consistent with re-evaluating already-feed-synced data — buildable today, no CAI-034 dependency). But AC5/AC10's "blocked at backend level from processing" describes exactly the cart→checkout transition moment that cart.md §6/CAI-034 covers, and per CAI-034's own Open Item, the real-time NewStore/MuleSoft flow for that moment **does not exist** ("will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed"). The ticket neither cites CAI-034 nor states which of the two mechanisms "blocked at backend level" is meant to be — this should be made explicit before build, given it changes the complexity and reliability characteristics of the CTA-blocking behaviour materially (guaranteed-current vs. up-to-15-minutes-stale).

---

### Overlap check against SFCC-796

**Distinct, correctly scoped — confirmed via 796's own description**, not inferred: SFCC-796 ("Cart Page – Product Unavailable," also status Tech design) explicitly states *"It does not cover inventory going out of stock (covered in SFCC-282) — this specifically covers the scenario where the product or variant is no longer active on the storefront but remains in the customer's bag."* Key behavioural difference it names: Wishlist is disabled for 796's scenario (product genuinely gone from catalogue) but remains available for 282's OOS/limited-stock scenario. 796 also states "checkout CTA is enabled" with no "blocked at backend" caveat — a simpler, cleaner statement than 282's contested AC5/AC10, worth using as a reference point when resolving 282's CTA-state question.

Two secondary notes:
- 796 depends on **SFCC-816** ("Cart Summary Component UI") where 282 depends on **SFCC-795** ("Cart Item Component UI (Part 2)") — worth confirming these are genuinely two different components, not naming drift on one.
- pdp.md's PRD-010 "Unavailable (size-level)" state (a still-active product with one OOS size, triggering Notify-Me) is a **narrower/different** meaning of "Unavailable" than SFCC-796's (whole product/variant deactivated in Business Manager). The ticket-level split between 282/796 is clean regardless, but be aware the term "Unavailable" isn't used consistently across the PRD and these two tickets.

---

### Specific questions to raise

- **[BA/PO — Emma Kirwan or Isabel Chaloner]** Which is correct on Checkout CTA state: the PRD requirement this ticket is labelled against (cart.md CAI-036: "disabled"), AC5/AC10 ("visually enabled... blocked at backend"), or the attached mockup (Checkout greyed, Apple Pay/Google Pay enabled)? AC5/AC10 need correcting either way.
- **[BA]** Confirm surface scope: mini-cart drawer only, full Cart Page only, or both — description/mockup say drawer, 3 of 4 dependency tickets say "Cart Page."
- **[Architecture/Integration team]** Confirm the mechanism behind "blocked at backend level from processing": SFCC validating its own feed-synced inventory (buildable now) vs. the unbuilt CAI-034 real-time flow. If feed-based, what staleness window (up to 15 min) is acceptable between a variant going OOS and checkout actually blocking it?
- **[Dev]** What does the shopper see/experience when they actually click Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay while "blocked at backend level"? No AC specifies an error response, message, or redirect.
- **[Dev/UX]** Confirm expected screen-reader/live-region behaviour for the three dynamically-appearing error surfaces (WCAG 2.2 4.1.3) before build — not in any AC currently.
- **[BA]** Is a mobile/narrow-viewport design forthcoming, or is desktop-only confirmed for this story at this stage?
- **[BA/Dev]** Confirm SFCC-795 vs SFCC-816 are genuinely distinct components.

---

### Readiness call

**Not ready to pull into a sprint** — PO sign-off and all 14 ACs exist, but the Checkout-CTA-state conflict (AC vs. PRD vs. design) and the CAI-034 real-time-vs-feed scoping are both unresolved, a11y/status-message handling is unaddressed, and all four dependency components (SFCC-795/404/274/275) remain in Tech design/In Refinement with none built — resolve those first, then re-size.
